inputs.share_count_basis: 1,212.2m ordinary shares in issue at 31 March 2026 (post the November 2025 ~GBP2bn placing; FY2026 AR note 22) plus 1.8m dilutive share awards (diluted weighted average 1,147.2m vs basic 1,145.4m, note 11.2). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and the company buys shares in the market to satisfy awards (GBP25.4m FY2026). Scrip dividend issuance is value-neutral in an unlevered DCF and is not modelled. The FY2026 weighted average (1,145.4m) is NOT used -- it predates the placing.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 AR consolidated cash flow statement, share-based payments add-back GBP29.6m; no net-share-settlement tax line disclosed (awards satisfied by market purchases, GBP25.4m in financing). SBC is immaterial (0.3% of revenue) so house and street bases nearly coincide.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts model GBP/share to quote pence. No FX market rate involved; no dual listing to parity-check. Per-share values in the JSON are in pence to match current_price.
inputs.net_debt_note: Consolidated basis: loans and borrowings GBP9,664.5m (current 1,204.4 + non-current 8,916.8 less leases) + lease liabilities GBP456.7m = total_debt GBP10,121.2m, less cash GBP1,542.9m = GBP8,578.3m. This deliberately INCLUDES the GBP1,258.4m of borrowings attributable to the SSEN Transmission 25% minority (the NCI claim is deducted in the bridge net of that debt) and EXCLUDES the GBP2,985.8m hybrid equity, which is deducted separately in the bridge. Company APM 'adjusted net debt and hybrid capital' GBP10,095.0m (note 1.2 / line 16512) nets leases and NCI debt and adds hybrids; the two reconcile: 8,578.3 - 456.7 leases - 1,258.4 NCI debt + 2,985.8 hybrid - 250.6 collateral/other = ~10,095 (within rounding of the collateral adjustment). H1 FY2027 trading update (1 Oct 2026) guides adjusted net debt and hybrid capital ~GBP11.5bn at 30 Sep 2026 -- the increase is the planned capex, which the forecast negative FCF already carries; the bridge therefore stays on the 31 Mar 2026 audited balance sheet.
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP build for GBP flows. Risk-free: UK 10y gilt ~4.5% (Oct 2026). ERP 5.0%, equity beta ~0.65 for a ~75%-networks-by-EBITDA utility (FY2030) -> cost of equity ~7.75%. Pre-tax cost of debt 4.75% (period-end average cost 4.1% incl. hybrid coupons; marginal sterling issuance ~5%), 3.6% post-tax at 25%. Target debt weight 40% (net debt + hybrids / EV rises from ~28% today toward the 4.5x ND/EBITDA ceiling management guides to through the plan) -> CAPM WACC ~6.1%. Rounded UP to 6.5% because ~30% of EBITDA (Renewables, Thermal, Energy Markets) carries merchant price and wind-volume exposure that a pure-network beta understates, and because Ofgem's RIIO-3 allowed nominal WACC (~4.3-4.5% CPIH-real, ~6.5% nominal) is the rate at which the regulated growth capex is value-neutral. One WACC across all three scenarios; risk is charged in the flows (adaptations rule f), not stacked in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt: lease liabilities GBP456.7m sit inside total_debt; lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows; lease interest is below EBITDA. Right-of-use renewal (~GBP87m/yr principal, 0.85% of revenue) is immaterial against GBP5-8bn/yr capex and is absorbed in the capex path. lease_cost_pct_path is 0.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge. The DCF consolidates 100% of SSEN Transmission (Ontario Teachers' holds 25%). The NCI claim is deducted in equity_bridge at an estimated fair value of GBP1,400m: 25% x SSEN Transmission gross RAV GBP8,955m (31 Mar 2026) at ~1.2x RAV premium, less the GBP1,258.4m of consolidated debt attributable to NCI holders (note 1.2 line 12563) that is already inside net_debt. Book NCI is GBP751.6m; the 2022 OTPP transaction implied a RAV premium, so book understates the claim. Because regulated growth capex earns approximately the regulatory WACC (NPV ~0 at the model WACC), 25% of Transmission's future consolidated flows is worth approximately the NCI's present fair value -- deducting it today is the consistent one-shot charge. Flows are left gross (not attributable-only). Hybrid equity GBP2,985.8m is ALSO deducted in the bridge as a debt-like claim: its coupons (GBP72.9m FY2026, rising after the FY2026 GBP1.1bn issuance) are paid below the line and are not in the flows.
inputs.jv_treatment: Equity-accounted JVs (Dogger Bank, Seagreen, Beatrice etc.): the share of JV profit after tax is inside adjusted operating profit and JV D&A (GBP173.0m) is added back in adjusted EBITDA (GBP3,207.9m), so JV cash generation is in the flows and JV project-finance debt is serviced inside them (not added to net debt). Interest on SSE's shareholder loans to JVs is finance income (below EBITDA, excluded from the flows), so by the matching-asset rule the loans to JVs and associates (GBP1,621.2m at book, note 16) are ADDED in the bridge. Equity investments in JVs (GBP1,945.1m) are NOT added -- their earnings are already in the flows.
inputs.ebitda_basis: Adjusted EBITDA APM GBP3,207.9m FY2026 (31.5% of revenue): adjusted operating profit GBP2,236.6m + D&A before exceptional charges GBP879.3m + JV share of D&A GBP173.0m - depreciation on fair-value uplifts GBP20.3m - release of deferred income GBP13.1m - NCI share of D&A GBP47.6m (note 5.1(v)). Statutory operating profit and net income are swamped by derivative re-measurements (FY2023 statutory OP -GBP146m) and are not used. D&A for the tax line is consolidated + JV D&A (~GBP1,052m, 10.3% of revenue).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 2, operating company non-US, with adaptations a1 GBP WACC, a2 GBP->GBp quote, b leases-as-debt, c NCI in bridge, d JV-loan matching asset). SSE is an operating utility, not a REIT/bank/holdco, so no non-FCF route applies; the AIA.NZ capex-supercycle precedent (10-year explicit horizon with capex tapering to a steady-state multiple of D&A, growth capex at regulated returns treated as value-neutral beyond the horizon) is followed. Reported FCF is structurally negative (-GBP1,008m FY2026) and will stay negative through ~FY2032 under the GBP33bn FY2026-30 plan (SSEN Transmission ~GBP22bn, Distribution ~GBP5bn, Renewables/Flex ~GBP6bn); the DCF funds that from the forecast negative flows (i.e. future debt and the Nov-2025 placing already in the share count), and the terminal value capitalises the enlarged asset base. TERMINAL: Gordon at 6.5%/2.5% is 25.6x FCF; the house default 20x cap is raised to 22x base (utility, ~80% of FY2030 EBITDA index-linked; 22x terminal FCF equals ~9.9x terminal EBITDA, inside the UK-utility 9-11x range), 25x bull, 20x bear -- the cap binds in every scenario, so terminal_growth is a disclosure not a driver. TAX: cash tax paid was only GBP61m FY2026 (adjusted current tax rate 9.6%) because of UK full expensing on the capex programme; the cash rate is ramped from 8% to the 25% statutory rate only as capex tapers (FY2035+). Electricity Generator Levy was raised to 55% in 2026 (Analysis JSON); it sits above EBIT in the adjusted current-tax rate and is absorbed in the cash-tax ramp, not modelled separately. SBC-light market: SBC kept explicit at 0.3% of revenue. ANCHORS: price is the 9 Oct 2026 regular close (not after-hours); balance sheet and share count are the 31 Mar 2026 audited year-end, the latest published (H1 FY2027 results due 18 Nov 2026 -- refresh net debt, hybrid balance and share count then). GUIDANCE used: FY2027 adjusted EPS 168-193p (reiterated 1 Oct 2026, H1 64-68p), FY2030 225-250p (10-13% CAGR from FY2026 restated 153.5p), ND/EBITDA below 4.5x through the plan, SSEN Transmission gross RAV GBP13bn FY2025 -> GBP40bn FY2030. Base case is pitched at the LOW end of guidance (FY2027 ~170p, FY2030 ~228p); bull at/above the top; bear ~185p FY2030. Analysis JSON (landed during the build) corroborates the axes used; narratives are drawn from it and from the FY2026 annual report, the Q1 FY2027 statement and the 1 Oct 2026 trading update.
inputs.owner_fcf_margin_check: FY2026 actual owner FCF margin -10.2% (capex 43.6% of revenue). Year-1 component build gives ~-16% (capex 51%): lower, not higher, than the latest actual, so nothing unrepeatable is being carried forward. Margin turns positive FY2033 and matures at ~21% by FY2036 as capex settles at ~1.25x D&A.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Year-1 base revenue growth; anchored to management's FY2026-30 adjusted EPS CAGR guidance of 10-13% (haircut to the low end) and RIIO-T3 allowed-revenue growth, not to the historical series
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (14-19%) diverges >30% from revenue (-6.6%/+8.3%) and adjusted-profit (-5.5%/+10.3%) CAGRs. Equity is inflated by the Nov-2025 ~GBP2bn placing and FY2022-23 hedge-reserve swings; revenue is dominated by energy pass-through and the FY2023 commodity spike (GBP12.5bn) and says little about earnings power. Neither series is a usable forward growth proxy; guidance and RAV growth are used instead.
historical_growth.notes: EPS CAGRs use ProfitBeforeExceptionalsAttributable (kpis), not statutory EPS, which is swamped by derivative re-measurements (FY2020 and FY2023 statutory losses). Owner FCF is negative in 4 of the last 5 years (capex supercycle), so FCF CAGRs are undefined and omitted. Owner FCF history (reported FCF - SBC): FY2021 621.8, FY2022 151.3, FY2023 -340.8, FY2024 1,327.3, FY2025 -676.5, FY2026 -1,038.0.

base.capex_note: GBP: FY27 5.5bn, FY28 6.5bn, FY29 7.5bn, FY30 8.0bn (FY26-30 cash capex ~GBP31.9bn + JV funding ~= the GBP33bn plan; FY27 guided 'over GBP5bn', H1 FY27 ~GBP2.5bn), then ED3/T4 taper: FY31 7.0, FY32 6.0, FY33 5.0, FY34 4.2, FY35 3.3, FY36 2.75bn (= 1.25x D&A, i.e. ~2.5% nominal RAV growth in the terminal year).
base.margin_note: FY27 37% -> adjusted EBITDA ~GBP4.0bn, consistent with ~170p adjusted EPS (low end of 168-193p). FY30 44.5% -> ~GBP5.7bn EBITDA, ~228p (low end of 225-250p). Mix shift to Transmission (RIIO-T3 from Apr-26, RAV 9 -> 40bn gross) and Distribution ED3 (Apr-28) drives the margin, not pass-through revenue.

bull.capex_note: Slightly higher absolute capex (Berwick Bank consented, extra Renewables/Flex: FY27 5.6bn ... FY30 8.3bn, FY36 2.95bn) on a larger revenue base.

bear.capex_note: Committed Transmission capex is largely non-discretionary so early-year absolute capex is only modestly lower (FY27 5.4bn ... FY30 7.2bn); overruns above allowances are not remunerated, which is why EBITDA is lower while capex is not.

scenario_narratives.base: Management delivers the GBP33bn FY2026-30 plan broadly on time: SSEN Transmission's 11 major ASTI/LOTI projects energise within RIIO-T3 allowances, gross RAV reaches ~GBP40bn by FY2030 and ~80% of group EBITDA is index-linked. Adjusted EPS lands at the low end of guidance (~170p FY2027, ~228p FY2030) as Distribution's ED3 settlement (from April 2028) is adequate but not generous and renewables capture prices are average. Leverage peaks near but below 4.5x ND/EBITDA; no further equity is needed. Owner FCF is negative through FY2032 and the business is worth its enlarged regulated and contracted asset base at a ~10x terminal EBITDA multiple. Cash tax stays low under full expensing until capex tapers.
scenario_narratives.bull: Transmission RAV growth runs ahead of plan (T3 reopeners and accelerated grid connections), ED3 is set at RIIO-T3-like returns, the consented 4.1GW Berwick Bank reaches FID in 2027 with Phase A joining Phase B's AR7 CfD, Dogger Bank completes on schedule and wind yields and capture prices are favourable. Adjusted EPS reaches the top of the range (~195p FY2027, ~250p+ FY2030), the market pays a UK-network RAV premium (25x terminal FCF, ~11x EBITDA) and the group's index-linked earnings re-rate as gilt yields ease.
scenario_narratives.bear: Ofgem's ED3 determination cuts allowed returns, Transmission cost overruns and supply-chain delays (HVDC cables, consents) fall outside allowances, renewables output and capture prices disappoint (CfD/zonal-pricing policy uncertainty), and higher-for-longer gilt yields raise financing cost faster than indexation compensates. Adjusted EPS stalls near ~160p FY2027 and ~185p FY2030, leverage tests the 4.5x ceiling and the dividend or a second equity raise is on the table. Terminal exit at 20x FCF (~8x EBITDA, the 2022-23 UK-utility sector trough; UK networks have not traded below ~1.0x RAV even under stress, which a lower multiple would imply) reflects a de-rated UK utility sector.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 25%: the equity story rests on a single regulator's (Ofgem) ED3 and T3 settlements, the plan is funded to the edge of the 4.5x ND/EBITDA guardrail, and a regulated utility with GBP33bn of committed capex has little room to cut if returns or allowances disappoint. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because reaching the top of guidance needs several independent things to go right at once (regulatory returns, project delivery, wind yield, capture prices, consents). Base 50%: management has a record of hitting adjusted-EPS guidance ranges and the FY2027 range was reiterated on 1 Oct 2026.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Unlevered owner-FCF DCF through a regulated capex supercycle: ten explicit years of negative-then-recovering free cash flow at a GBP nominal WACC of 6.5%, terminal value capped at a utility exit multiple, with hybrid capital and the Transmission minority deducted as claims and JV shareholder loans added as a matching asset. Growth capex at regulated returns is treated as value-neutral beyond the horizon, so the value is the enlarged asset base in place by FY2036, not a bet on perpetual RAV growth. The market price above the base IV is the RAV premium / growth-at-above-WACC-returns the market is prepared to pay; the required-return table shows what discount rate the price implies.
key_risks_to_valuation: Regulatory: Ofgem ED3 (2028-33) and T3 reopeners set the return on ~75% of FY2030 EBITDA; a 50bp cut in allowed return on a GBP40bn+ RAV is ~GBP150-200m of EBIT
Delivery: 11 major Transmission projects (ASTI/LOTI) with HVDC supply-chain and consenting risk; overruns above allowances are shareholder cost
Funding: ND/EBITDA guided below 4.5x; a slip in EBITDA or capex phasing forces dividend rebasing or a second equity raise (dilution not in the flat share count)
Merchant exposure: ~30% of EBITDA (Renewables, Thermal, Energy Markets) depends on wind yield, capture prices and capacity-market/CfD policy
Rates: a 1pp move in gilt yields moves both WACC and allowed returns; the model's terminal cap (22x FCF) binds, so value is more sensitive to the exit multiple than to terminal growth
Bridge estimates: NCI fair value (GBP1.4bn) and JV loans at book are judgement; each GBP500m is ~41p/share
Terminal dependence: with negative interim flows the terminal value exceeds 100% of enterprise value; the valuation is a view on FY2036 steady-state FCF and its multiple
valuation_philosophy.entry_price_interpretation: The 15%-hurdle entry price is NEGATIVE in every scenario (weighted about -830p) and the required-return table turns negative above ~10%: with six years of negative owner FCF and GBP11.6bn of net debt plus hybrids ahead of the equity, no positive purchase price delivers a 15% IRR under the plan. This is the finding, not an error: SSE is a 6-7% nominal-IRR regulated asset, and the sensitivity grid shows the current price implies a discount rate of roughly 5% at a 22x exit multiple (4.5% WACC -> 2,648p, 5.5% -> 2,275p). The terminal cap binds in all scenarios so terminal growth is not a driver; WACC and the exit multiple are.
